title: Tamiloid languages - Wikipedia
text: The Tamiloid languages, also known as the Tamil languages, are the group of Dravidian languages most closely related to Tamil. In addition to Tamil itself, they are Eravallan, Kaikadi, Mala Malasar, Malasar, Malapandaram, Mannan, Muthuvan, Paliyan, Pattapu, Bugandi and Yerukala.

title: Mala Malasar | Ethnologue Free
text: Mala Malasar is a stable indigenous language of India. It belongs to the Dravidian language family. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community.

title: Mala Malasar language — Grokipedia
text: The Mala Malasar language, a member of the Southern Dravidian branch, features consonants attested in a 2002 sociolinguistic survey's wordlist transcriptions, including stops, nasals, fricatives, affricates, laterals, rhotics, and approximants across multiple places of articulation.
